key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and identify lead-free double-perovskite architectures with very high predicted efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The study offers actionable design rules for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations to optimize charge extraction and reduce recombination in next-generation perovskite solar cells.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors: HTL band gap, absorber band gap, and ETL electron affinity.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable rank prediction, and full SCAPS-1D verification confirmed top candidates such as FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on simulation-based screening and should still be validated experimentally, especially for fabrication tolerances and interface quality.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
